units.en: Military Guards, Part 3 — Five Capitals Militia Levies
units.literal: Military Guards, Part 3 ○ Five Capitals Militia Levies

units.zh: 遼建五京：臨潢，契丹故壤；
units.en: The Liao founded five capitals—Linhuang in the old Khitan heartland;
units.literal: Liao established five capitals: Linhuang, the old Khitan homeland;

units.zh: 遼陽，漢之遼東，為渤海故國；
units.en: Liaoyang, the Han Liaodong region and former Bohai state;
units.literal: Liaoyang, Han-era Liaodong, the former Bohai realm;

units.zh: 中京，漢遼西地，自唐以來契丹有之。
units.en: Zhongjing in Han Liaoxi, which the Khitan had held since Tang.
units.literal: Zhongjing, Han Liaoxi territory, held by the Khitan since Tang times.

units.zh: 三京丁籍可紀者二十二萬六千一百，蕃漢轉戶為多。
units.en: Among the three capitals, registrable levies came to 226,100—mostly Fan and Han rotating households.
units.literal: The three capitals' registrable ding totaled two hundred twenty-six thousand one hundred; Fan and Han rotating households were the majority.

units.zh: 析津、大同、故漢地，籍丁八十萬六千七百。
units.en: Former Han districts such as Xijin and Datong listed 806,700 militia levies.
units.literal: Xijin, Datong, and other former Han lands registered eight hundred six thousand seven hundred ding.

units.zh: 契丹本戶多隸宮帳、部族，其餘蕃漢戶丁分隸者，皆不與焉。
units.en: Khitan core families mostly fell under palace tents and tribes, so other Fan and Han levies assigned elsewhere were excluded from these rolls.
units.literal: Most native Khitan households were attached to palace tents and tribes; other Fan and Han household ding assigned elsewhere were not included.

units.en: Taizu founded the imperial capital at Linhuang Prefecture.
units.literal: Taizu built the imperial capital at Linhuang Prefecture.

units.zh: 太宗定晉，晉主石敬瑭來獻十六城，乃定四京，改皇都為上京。
units.en: When Taizong pacified Jin, Shi Jingtang of Later Jin ceded sixteen prefectures; the court then fixed four capitals and renamed the imperial seat Shangjing.
units.literal: Taizong settled Jin; Jin ruler Shi Jingtang presented sixteen prefectures, then four capitals were fixed and the imperial capital was renamed Shangjing.

units.zh: 有丁一十六萬七千二百。
units.literal: It had one hundred sixty-seven thousand two hundred ding.

units.en: Linhuang Prefecture — Linhuang County registered 7,000 militia levies.
At Zu Prefecture, Changba County counted 4,000 militia levies.
At Huai Prefecture, Fuyu County counted 3,000 militia levies.

units.zh: 慶州玄寧縣丁一萬二千。
units.en: Qing Prefecture — Xuanning County: 12,000 militia levies.

units.zh: 泰州興國縣丁一千四百。
units.en: Tai Prefecture — Xingguo County: 1,400 militia levies.
Changchun Prefecture — Changchun County: 4,000 militia levies.
Wu Prefecture — Aimin County: 2,000 militia levies.
At Yong Prefecture, Changning County counted 9,000 militia levies.
Yikun Prefecture — Guangyi County: 5,000 militia levies.
Longhua Prefecture — Longhua County: 2,000 militia levies.

units.zh: 降聖州永安縣丁一千五百。
units.en: Jiangsheng Prefecture — Yongan County: 1,500 militia levies.
At Rao Prefecture, Changle County counted 8,000 militia levies.
Under the court's direct retainers, Hui Prefecture listed 20,000 militia levies.

units.zh: 東京，本渤海，以其地建南京遼陽府。
units.en: The Eastern Capital began as Bohai; the Liao built Nanjing Liaoyang Prefecture on that ground.
units.literal: Eastern Capital: originally Bohai; its territory became Nanjing Liaoyang Prefecture.

units.zh: 統縣六，轄軍、府、州、城二十六，有丁四萬一千四百。
units.en: It ruled six counties and twenty-six military prefectures and cities, with 41,400 levies on the rolls.
units.literal: It governed six counties, twenty-six armies, prefectures, and walled posts, with forty-one thousand four hundred ding.

units.zh: 天顯十三年，太宗改為東京。
units.en: In Tianxian year 13 Taizong redesignated it the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianxian, Taizong renamed it Eastern Capital.

units.en: Liaoyang Prefecture — Liaoyang County registered 3,000 militia levies.
At Kai Prefecture, Kaiyuan County counted 2,000 militia levies.

units.zh: 定州：定東縣丁一千六百。
units.en: At Ding Prefecture, Dingdong County counted 1,600 militia levies.
At Bao Prefecture, Laiyuan County counted 2,000 militia levies.

units.zh: 南京析津府，統縣十一，轄軍、府、州、城九，有丁五十六萬六千。
units.en: Nanjing's Xijin Prefecture held eleven counties and nine subordinate commands, listing 566,000 militia levies.
units.literal: Southern Capital Xijin Prefecture governed eleven counties, nine armies, prefectures, and cities, with five hundred sixty-six thousand ding.

units.en: Xijin Prefecture — Xijin County registered 40,000 militia levies.
Shun Prefecture — Huairou County: 10,000 militia levies.
At Tan Prefecture, Miyun County counted 10,000 militia levies.
At Zhuo Prefecture, Fanyang County counted 20,000 militia levies.
At Yi Prefecture, Yi County counted 50,000 militia levies.
At Ji Prefecture, Yuyang County counted 8,000 militia levies.

units.zh: 平州：盧龍縣丁一萬四千。
units.en: At Ping Prefecture, Lulong County counted 14,000 militia levies.
At Luan Prefecture, Yifeng County counted 8,000 militia levies.
At Ying Prefecture, Guangning County counted 6,000 militia levies.
At Jing Prefecture, Zunhua County counted 6,000 militia levies.

units.zh: 西京大同府，統縣七，轄軍、府、州、城十七，有丁三十二萬二千七百。
units.en: Xijing Datong Prefecture ruled seven counties and seventeen military jurisdictions, with 322,700 levies recorded.
units.literal: Western Capital Datong Prefecture governed seven counties, seventeen armies, prefectures, and cities, with three hundred twenty-two thousand seven hundred ding.

units.en: Datong Prefecture — Datong County registered 20,000 militia levies.
At Hong Prefecture, Yongning County counted 20,000 militia levies.
At De Prefecture, Xuande County counted 6,000 militia levies.

units.zh: 豐州：富民縣丁二千四百。
units.en: At Feng Prefecture, Fumin County counted 2,400 militia levies.
Zhenwu County raised 300 militia levies of local militia.

units.zh: 奉聖州：永興縣丁一萬六千。
units.en: At Fengsheng Prefecture, Yongxing County counted 16,000 militia levies.
At Guihua Prefecture, Wende County counted 20,000 militia levies.
At Kehan Prefecture, Huailai County counted 6,000 militia levies.
At Ru Prefecture, Jinshan County counted 10,000 militia levies.
At Yu Prefecture, Lingxian County counted 40,000 militia levies.

units.zh: 應州：金城縣丁一萬六千。
units.en: At Ying Prefecture, Jincheng County counted 16,000 militia levies.
At Shuo Prefecture, Shanyang County counted 8,000 militia levies.
The Jinsu Army posted 1,000 troops for autumn defense.
units.literal: Jinsu Army autumn-defense troops, one thousand.

units.en: At Wu Prefecture, Shenwu County counted 10,000 militia levies.
The Heqing Army likewise fielded 1,000 autumn-defense troops.
units.literal: Heqing Army autumn-defense troops, one thousand.

units.zh: 聖宗統和二十三年，城七金山，建大定府，號中京。
units.en: Shengzong's Tonghe year 23 saw Qijin Mountain fortified and Zhongjing established at Dading Prefecture.
units.literal: In the twenty-third year of Tonghe, Shengzong walled Qijin Mountain and founded Zhongjing at Dading Prefecture.

units.zh: 統縣九，轄軍、府、州、城二十三。
units.en: Zhongjing governed nine counties and twenty-three military prefectures and posts.
units.literal: It governed nine counties and twenty-three armies, prefectures, and cities.

units.zh: 草創末定，丁籍莫考，可見者一縣：高州三韓縣丁一萬。
units.en: Because the seat was newly founded, levies were not fully tallied; only Gaozhou's Sanhan County is recorded at 10,000 ding.
units.literal: Still in early founding and not yet fixed; ding rolls were unverified—only one county is visible: Gaozhou Sanhan County, ten thousand ding.

units.zh: 大約五京民丁可見者，一百一十萬七千三百為鄉兵。
units.en: In all, the Five Capitals' visible militia rolls came to about 1,107,300 levies.
units.literal: Roughly, visible militia ding of the Five Capitals totaled one million one hundred seven thousand three hundred.

units.zh: 遼屬國可紀者五十有九，朝貢無常。
units.en: Fifty-nine subject states appear in the records, though tribute missions had no fixed schedule.
units.literal: Liao subject states that can be recorded number fifty-nine; tribute audiences were irregular.

units.zh: 有事則遣使征兵，或下詔專征；
units.en: In emergencies the court dispatched envoys to raise troops or issued edicts ordering separate expeditions;
units.literal: When affairs arose the court sent envoys to levy troops, or issued edicts for dedicated campaigns;

units.en: States that refused were punished by force.
units.literal: Those who did not comply were attacked.

units.zh: 助軍眾寡，各從其便，無常額。
units.en: Contributed forces followed each realm's means, with no standing quota.
units.literal: Auxiliary forces varied in size at each state's convenience; there was no fixed quota.

units.zh: 又有鐵不得國者，興宗重熙十七年乞以兵助攻夏國，詔不許。
units.en: In Xingzong's Chongxi year 17 the Iron-Forbidden State once asked to join an attack on Western Xia; the court denied the request.
units.literal: There was also the Iron-Forbidden State: in Xingzong's Chongxi year 17 it begged troops to assist the attack on Western Xia; the edict refused.

units.zh: 遼之為國，鄰於梁、唐、晉、漢、周、宋。
units.en: Liao bordered in turn Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, Zhou, and Song.
units.literal: As a state Liao neighbored Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, Zhou, and Song.

units.zh: 晉以恩故，始則父子一家，終則寇讎相攻；
units.en: With Later Jin the bond began as kin-by-grace yet closed in mutual raids;
units.literal: Jin began as father and son in one household because of favor, yet ended with raiding and mutual attack;

units.en: Liang, Tang, and Zhou each stood as a full rival power.
units.literal: Liang, Tang, and Zhou were plainly one enemy state each.

units.zh: 宋惟太宗征北漢，遼不能救，餘多敗衄，縱得亦不償失。
units.en: Only when Song's Taizong campaigned against Northern Han could Liao not save it; otherwise Song mostly lost, and even victories did not repay the cost.
units.literal: Song only in Taizong's northern Han campaign did Liao fail to save them; most other clashes ended in defeat, and even victories did not repay the cost.

units.zh: 良由石晉獻土，中國失五關之固然也。
units.en: The root cause was Shi Jingtang's land grant and the Central States' forfeiture of the five passes' natural defenses.
units.literal: This truly stemmed from Shi Jingtang's cession of territory and China's loss of the five passes' natural strength.

units.zh: 高麗小邦，屢喪遼兵，非以險阻足恃故歟。
units.en: Small Goryeo still drained Liao forces again and again—perhaps its rugged ground alone could explain it.
units.literal: Goryeo was a small state yet repeatedly cost Liao armies—was it not because its difficult terrain was sufficient to rely on?

units.zh: 西夏彈丸之地，南敗宋，東抗遼。
units.en: Western Xia, though minute, beat Song to the south and held Liao at bay in the east.
units.literal: Western Xia was a tiny realm yet defeated Song in the south and resisted Liao in the east.

units.zh: 雖西北士馬雄勁，元昊、諒祚智勇過人，能使党項、阻卜掣肘大國，蓋亦襟山帶河，有以助其勢耳。
units.en: Even with strong northwestern cavalry, Yuanhao and Liangzuo's talent let Tangut and Zubu allies tie down a great empire, aided by mountains and rivers at their flank.
units.literal: Though northwestern horses and warriors were strong, Yuanhao and Liangzuo were surpassingly clever and brave, enabling Tangut and Zubu forces to check a great power—surely mountains and rivers at their backs helped their momentum.

units.zh: 雖然，宋久失地利，而舊《志》言兵，唯以敵宋為務。
units.en: Yet Song had lost terrain for years while older records still framed warfare chiefly against Song.
units.literal: Even so, Song long lacked terrain advantage, yet the old Monograph on troops treated Song alone as the enemy.

units.zh: 逾三關，聚議北京，猶不敢輕進。
units.en: Even after crossing the three passes and gathering councils at Beijing, Liao hesitated to push forward.
units.literal: Crossing three passes and massing councils at Beijing, they still dared not advance lightly.

units.zh: 豈不以大河在前，三鎮在後，臨事好謀之審，不容不然歟。
units.en: With the Yellow River ahead and the three prefectures behind, cautious planning at the crisis point left no other choice.
units.literal: Was it not because the Yellow River lay ahead and the three garrisons behind, and careful counsel at the moment could not permit otherwise?

units.zh: 二帳、十二宮一府、五京，有兵一百六十四萬二千八百。
units.en: Two imperial camps, twelve palaces, one office, and five capitals together fielded 1,642,800 troops.
units.literal: The two camps, twelve palaces, one office, and five capitals had troops totaling one million six hundred forty-two thousand eight hundred.

units.zh: 宮丁、大首領、諸部族，中京、頭下等州，屬國之眾，皆不與焉。
units.en: Palace levies, great chieftains, tribal hosts, Zhongjing, head-of-household domains, and subject troops lay outside this tally.
units.literal: Palace ding, great chieftains, all tribes, Zhongjing, subordinate prefectures, and subject peoples were not included.

units.en: Restraint in committing them was how the dynasty lasted.
units.literal: Not deploying them lightly was how the dynasty endured long.

units.zh: 又得高麗《大遼事跡》，載東境戌兵，以備高麗、女直等國，見其守國規模，布置簡要，舉一可知三邊矣。
units.en: From Goryeo's record of Great Liao Affairs we also learn eastern garrisons facing Goryeo and Jurchen—a concise frontier layout from which all three borders can be inferred.
units.literal: Goryeo's Great Liao Affairs also records eastern-border garrison troops against Goryeo, Jurchen, and other states—showing how the frontier was held in brief, telling arrangement; one example reveals all three borders.

units.zh: 東京至鴨淥西北峰為界：黃龍府正兵五千。
units.en: The Eastern Capital frontier to the Yalu's northwest ridge: 5,000 regulars at Huanglong Prefecture.
units.literal: From Eastern Capital to the Yalu's northwest peaks as the border: Huanglong Prefecture regular troops five thousand.

units.zh: 東京沿女直界至鴨淥江：軍堡凡七十，各守軍二十人，計正兵一千四百。
units.en: From Eastern Capital along the Jurchen line to the Yalu stood seventy forts with twenty men each—1,400 regulars in all.
units.literal: Along the Jurchen border from Eastern Capital to the Yalu River: seventy forts in all, each holding twenty men, totaling one thousand four hundred regulars.

units.zh: 來遠城宣義軍營八：太子營正兵三百。
units.en: At Laiyuan's Xuanyi Army eight camps, the Crown Prince Camp held 300 regulars.
units.literal: Laiyuan City, Xuanyi Army, eight camps: Crown Prince Camp regular troops three hundred.

units.en: Great Camp: 600 militia levies of regulars.
Pu Prefecture Camp: 200 militia levies of regulars.
units.literal: Pu Prefecture Camp regular troops, 200 ding.

units.en: New Camp: 500 militia levies of regulars.
Jiata Camp: 500 militia levies of regulars.
Wanghai City garrisoned 300 militia levies of regulars.
Liubai Camp: 400 militia levies of regulars.
Woye Camp: 1,000 militia levies of regulars.
Shenhu City garrisoned 10,000 militia levies of regulars.
The post was founded in Dakang year 10.

units.zh: 右一府、一州、二城、七十堡、八營，計正兵二萬二千。
units.en: Totals: one prefecture, one zhou, two cities, seventy forts, eight camps—22,000 regular troops.
units.literal: Right: one prefecture, one zhou, two cities, seventy forts, eight camps—regular troops totaling twenty-two thousand.

findings.problem: Undated geographic-historical summaries and an evaluative sentence about Yuanhao and Liangzuo were expanded into point dates or full activity intervals without source wording that establishes those personal chronologies.
findings.action: Replace each unsupported point year or interval and the paired active hint with a source-specific unresolved hold. Retain the non-date historical/geographic content and leave the directly dated Taizong, Shengzong, and Xingzong evidence unchanged.
